headline: EU NAMES 46 STRATEGIC CRITICAL MINERAL PROJECTS — FAST-TRACK PERMITTING AND FINANCING PRIORITY FOR BATTERY AND DEFENSE METALS
snippet: The European Commission on October 9 designated 46 new 'Strategic Projects' under the Critical Raw Materials Act, covering lithium, rare earths, nickel, cobalt and other battery and defense-critical minerals across EU member states and partner countries. The designations grant fast-track permitting, priority access to EU financing instruments and supply-chain recognition — directly benefiting junior explorers with European-adjacent assets seeking off-take partners or strategic equity from European industrial buyers.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM RESTARTS GROTA DO CIRILO AFTER BRAZIL COURT REVERSES SUSPENSION — ONLY PRODUCING ASSET BACK ONLINE
snippet: Sigma Lithium resumed mining and processing at Grota do Cirilo — Brazil's largest spodumene operation and the company's only producing asset — after a federal appeals court (TRF-6) reinstated three environmental licences suspended September 4 at the request of the Quilombola community federation N'Golo. The underlying consultation dispute over the 8-km community boundary around the mine remains unresolved, meaning further legal challenges are possible even as the company reaffirms its target of reaching 330,000 tonnes/yr concentrate capacity by end-2027.

headline: Q2 METALS DRILLS 134.5M AT 1.20% LI2O AT CISCO — NEAR-SURFACE EXPANSION OUTLINES PIT GROWTH AHEAD OF PENDING PEA
snippet: Q2 Metals (TSXV: QTWO) reported hole CS26-096 at Cisco in James Bay, Quebec returned 134.5 metres averaging 1.20% Li2O from 11.8 metres depth — expanding near-surface mineralization outside the conceptual pit used in the April resource. A companion hole cut 29.2 metres at 1.53% Li2O including a 19.3-metre core at 1.84% Li2O, as Q2 advances a multi-rig 2026 summer program with a Preliminary Economic Assessment expected this fall. The 11-metre start depth underscores the near-surface economics critical to any open-pit PEA case.

headline: ROCK TECH LITHIUM SLASHES ONTARIO REFINERY COST 54% TO C$596M — REVISED ECONOMICS DRAMATICALLY IMPROVE PROJECT VIABILITY
snippet: Rock Tech Lithium (TSXV: RCK) cut the capital cost estimate for its Georgian Bay lithium hydroxide refinery in Ontario to C$596 million (US$421 million) from a previous estimate exceeding C$1.3 billion — a 54% reduction driven by scope refinement, contractor negotiations and a value-engineering review. The revision materially improves the project's path to a financing decision and positions the Ontario plant as one of the more capital-competitive domestic lithium hydroxide options for North American EV supply chains.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING ACQUIRES McEWEN'S TIMMINS ASSETS FOR US$55M — FULLER PROJECT AND PAYMASTER JV ADD TO PAMOUR COMPLEX
snippet: Discovery Mining (TSX: DSV) signed an asset purchase agreement to acquire McEwen Mining's Fuller project and a 60% interest in the Paymaster Joint Venture in Timmins, Ontario for US$55 million — US$50 million in common shares and US$5 million cash at closing. The acquisition adds surface and underground potential adjacent to Discovery's existing Pamour operation, consolidating a meaningful land package around one of Ontario's most historically productive gold camps with closing expected before month-end, subject to royalty extinguishment and regulatory sign-off.

headline: USA RARE EARTH AND MP MATERIALS SLIDE 5% FOR SECOND STRAIGHT DAY — US-CHINA DIPLOMATIC THAW DEFLATES SUPPLY-CHAIN PREMIUM
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) fell another 5% on October 8 — its second consecutive session of 5% declines — while MP Materials (MP) dipped a further 5% and United States Antimony dropped 4%, with the sector declining at roughly five times the pace of broader equity markets. Analysts tie the two-day selloff to easing US-China diplomatic tensions that are quietly unwinding the supply-chain nationalism trade thesis: the same geopolitical fear that sent these stocks higher is now fading, raising questions about the valuation premium built on policy risk rather than operating fundamentals.

headline: URANIUM EQUITIES SLIDE 5-7% AS SECTOR DISCONNECTS FROM $90-$97/LB CONTRACT PRICES — DENISON LEADS DECLINE
snippet: Uranium equities suffered a broad selloff October 7-8, with Denison Mines (TSX: DML) falling 5.43% and Ur-Energy (TSX: URE) declining 7.05% even as spot uranium held near US$89.85/lb and long-term contract prices firmed to US$97/lb — a disconnect between physical prices and equity performance that analysts attribute to broader risk-off sentiment and profit-taking after the sector's summer run. Denison's Phoenix in-situ recovery project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin continues to advance toward full production, an upcoming catalyst that bulls argue the current equity weakness ignores.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: KINROSS CUTS GUIDANCE 8%, SHANDONG TRIMS TARGET 23% — COST HEADWINDS BITE TOP PRODUCERS EVEN AT $4,000+ GOLD
snippet: Frank Holmes' weekly Gold SWOT at GoldSeek flags two notable guidance reductions: Kinross Gold revised its 2026-2027 production outlook down 8% to 1.84-1.86 million ounces, and Shandong Gold cut its 2026 target to 36-38 tonnes from an original 49+ tonne guidance — a roughly 23% reduction — signalling that cost pressures and operational headwinds are meaningful even as gold holds above $4,000/oz. On the positive side, Ramelius Resources raised its FY2027-2030 production outlook by approximately 5%, illustrating the bifurcation between disciplined low-cost producers and those stretched by inflation and execution challenges.

headline: CANADA ONE MINING FINDS NEW HIGH-GRADE ZONE AT COPPER DOME BC — UP TO 4.08 G/T AU AND 3.92% CU IN SURFACE SAMPLING
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Canada One Mining (TSXV: CONE)
snippet: Canada One Mining (TSXV: CONE) reported 2026 summer reconnaissance results from Copper Dome in British Columbia, with Camp Zone rock sampling returning up to 4.08 g/t gold and 3.92% copper, and the identification of a previously unrecognized diabase unit with copper enrichment at Copper Dome South that management says warrants systematic follow-up. While rock-chip samples are not resource-equivalent, the gold-copper values from the new diabase zone represent a genuinely novel exploration target at a property previously drilled with less comprehensive geological mapping.
